pipeline_version: v5 (post department-head corrections + class-weighted loss fix)

exclusion_reasons: topical overlap with the paper's own domain (energy / time-series)
features without a semantic identity (raw pixels, pixel-derived transforms, digitizer stroke coordinates)
windowed sensor/signal data (same class as electricity, one level more general)
anonymized or unnamed features (identity-ablation question cannot be posed)
near-duplicate of another selected dataset under a different encoding (dna/splice)
phase1_dataset_selection.tabzilla_hard_overlap_flag_note: in_tabzilla_hard_unverified field reconstructed from secondary sources, not verified against github.com/naszilla/tabzilla byte-for-byte -- robustness annotation only, not a selection criterion

checks: numeric column >=95% missing in training fold
numeric column zero variance after median imputation
categorical column with a single category in training fold
actual official split sizes vs. Phase-1 80/20 estimate

official_split.note: Phase-1 n_test_est assumed an 80/20 split; official CC-18 folds are ~10-fold CV and turned out smaller -- see preflight/Phase-2 logged comparison per dataset

preprocessing.fit_on: training-sub fold only (no leakage into val/test)
preprocessing.numeric: median imputation (train-fold median; all-missing columns fall back to 0.0), then StandardScaler
preprocessing.categorical: OrdinalEncoder, unseen categories mapped to a dedicated bucket per column

model.ablated_component: per-feature identity bias b_j in the feature tokenizer T_j(x) = b_j + f_j(x)

optimization.training_loss: cross-entropy, class-weighted by inverse training-fold frequency (N / (K * N_class)); fixes majority-class collapse observed on 'sick' under unweighted loss

phase2_training.resumable: one artifacts/task_<id>_fold_0.npz per dataset; existing files skipped on rerun
known_deviations: sick (task 3021): initial run collapsed to majority-class prediction (val balanced acc = 0.5000 for all 5 seeds x 2 configs) due to an all-missing numeric column (median() of all-NaN column is NaN, silently reaching StandardScaler) compounded by severe class imbalance (~6% positive) under unweighted cross-entropy; fixed by (a) falling back missing-median columns to 0.0 and (b) class-weighted training loss; full 170 runs were then repeated (not just sick) since the loss-weighting change affects all datasets

phase3_analysis.completeness_gate: refuses to compute anything unless all 17 tasks have an artifact

variance_decomposition.reused_from: seed_window_simgrid.py (Section 3 of the revision package, unmodified)
variance_decomposition.window_definition: each individual test example is its own column (W = n_test); NOT synthetic 10-40 example blocks
variance_decomposition.block_length_rationale: CC-18 test examples are exchangeable (CC-18 excludes time series by construction); block=1 is an ordinary iid bootstrap, appropriate because there is no real neighbourhood structure to preserve, unlike the household/ECL time-window setting

primary.name: balanced error (percentage points)
primary.identity: mean(L_i) over the test fold equals 100 x (1 - balanced_accuracy) exactly (finite-sample identity, self-tested in code)

secondary.name: cross-entropy (sensitivity metric)
secondary.formula: per-example loss_ablated - loss_full, both raw model cross-entropy

phase3_analysis.degenerate_case_handling: exactly-zero variance in both components (sig2_seed and V_win) is flagged (degenerate_zero_variance=true) rather than raised; can be a genuine null result or a sign of an upstream degenerate run

phase4_flip_diagnostic.purpose: tests whether low balanced-error seed share correlates with a low argmax-flip rate between configs
phase4_flip_diagnostic.result_summary: weak-to-moderate correlation only (Pearson flip_rate vs balanced_error_seed_share = 0.40; balanced_error_seed_share vs cross_entropy_seed_share = 0.24) -- discretization is a contributing factor, not the dominant explanation; per-dataset share estimates at k=5 seeds are inherently noisy regardless of metric

phase5_pooling.method: random-effects meta-analysis, REML for between-dataset variance (tau^2), Hartung-Knapp adjustment for the pooled CI (t on k-1 df)
phase5_pooling.validated_against: statsmodels.stats.meta_analysis.combine_effects (Paule-Mandel + HKSJ) and a published textbook example (Borenstein et al., 2009, Table 12.2) -- pooled effect/CI matched to 3-4 decimal places in both a null-heterogeneity and a substantial-heterogeneity synthetic case
phase5_pooling.se_recovery: per-dataset SE recovered from the already-computed t4 CI: SE_i = (ci_hi_i - ci_lo_i) / (2 * t_{0.975,4}), not recomputed from raw data

balanced_error.note: naive-vs-HK discrepancy is a direct illustration of the paper's own t_{S-1}-vs-normal-quantile argument (Section 3.2), applied one level up at the pooling stage

environment.note: python/torch/cuda supplied by the user; openml is the package used to fetch OpenML-CC18 (suite id 99) via openml.study.get_suite(99)
